dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Some tiles come already placed. Build the rest around them, in order.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A LOOP repeats the line below it. 'for i in range(3)' runs that line three times.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Place the repeated line one tile RIGHT. That indent is what puts it inside the loop.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A FUNCTION is a named block. 'def greet' names it; the indented lines below are its body.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Defining it doesn't run it. Write its name on its own line below, back at the left wall.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A function can take an ARGUMENT — a value you hand it. 'def greet(name)' declares a slot called name.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Calling greet("Sam") fills that slot with "Sam". Inside the body, use the slot's name — not a quoted word.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Nothing is placed for you now. Every bracket and quote is yours to collect and put in order.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Nothing is lying on the floor in here. The words are being CARRIED — you have to take them.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A ! on a tile means one is arriving there. Until it finishes, it isn't really there — you can walk past it and you cannot hit it.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Once it is up, it blocks your way. Face it and press F to attack. Beat it and it drops the word it was holding — walk over the drop to take it.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Careful — something in here eats CODE, not you. It takes a word you already placed.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Once it's holding something, a ring appears under it. Beat it before the ring empties and it drops what it took.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: It just grabbed one of yours. Face it and press F before the ring runs out.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: An IF is a gate. The line indented under it only runs when the test holds.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: ELSE is the other road. It lines up with the if, and its own line is indented under it.
